title: Rules of the Line
summary: Nothing here is called a war, and there are things you do not do.
body: No one on Tessell has declared anything. Contracts are written as line maintenance, asset recovery, right-of-way enforcement. Employers prefer it that way and so do the free companies, because a war has sides and a maintenance dispute has invoices.
The conduit is not a target. Cut it and the towns downstream go dark, and the next four employers will have heard about it before your lance has finished cooling.

An ejected pilot walks home. Shoot the seat and no one will ever hire you again — not out of sentiment, but because everybody on this continent is somebody's future employer, and the pool of people who can drive one of these is smaller every year.
Salvage belongs to whoever holds the ground at dusk. Not to whoever killed it, and not to whoever was paying. Whoever is standing there when the light goes.
